newsitem.title: EGYPT: PLO official-Egypt Mideast peace moves will fail.
newsitem.headline: PLO official-Egypt Mideast peace moves will fail.

text.p: Senior Palestinian official Farouk Kaddoumi said on Saturday Egypt's mission to restart Middle East peace talks was doomed to failure because of Israel's intransigence and lack of credibility.

"Egypt's efforts to save the peace process will fail because of Israel's intransigent position and provocations," Kaddoumi told reporters during a brief stop in Cairo airport. He was due in Bahrain for a two-day official visit.

"Israel will not change its policies towards the Arabs and what it tells the Arabs no longer has any credibility. I don't expect Egypt will be doing any real mediating because its an Arab country too," said Kaddoumi, who heads the PLO's political (foreign affairs) department.
Palestinian-Israeli peace talks ground to a halt in March after the Jewish state started building a Jewish settlement on occupied Arab land in East Jerusalem.
The Palestinians say they will hold talks with Israel only when it stops work on the settlement while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to keep on building.

Egypt, which considers itself an unofficial sponsor of the talks, has recently stepped up efforts to bring both sides together. On Thursday, Egyptian envoy Osama el-Baz shuttled between Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to try to resolve the impasse.
Kaddoumi, known for his tough stance, also told reporters that the United States was losing its credibility as an honest broker of the peace talks it co-sponsored back in 1991.

Asked what he thought about a non-binding U.S. House of Representatives resolution saying that Jerusalem must remain Israel's undivided capital, Kaddoumi said: "Day by day, the United States is losing its credibility as a sponsor of the peace talks. This is just another example."

Palestinians say settlement building pre-empts final peace talks to be held on issues which include the status of Jerusalem. They also want the Arab eastern part of the city as a capital of their future state.
Clashes broke out in the West Bank on Saturday between Palestinians and Israeli troops and several demonstrators told Reuters they were protesting against the House of Representatives resolution.
